messages:
maya: quick flag 1: antlia21b (int4) canary popped OOMs on long chat generations. Seen on 4/6 canary VMs.
lucas: ugh. is this slowgen-specific?
maya: yes, patterns show fragmentation rising around 7-9k tokens. sample log: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating 3.1GB for kv_cache_slot`
jihoon: reproduction notes?
maya: used multi-turn history + max_new_tokens=12000 + batch_size=3 + prefetch true. mem snapshots attached -> free memory in small scattered chunks.
emma: hypothesis: int4 allocation granularity + prefetch is causing small-slab fragmentation. Two safe mitigations: (1) reduce default max_new_tokens for antlia21b; (2) reserve headroom per-instance before prefetch so requests hit reservation instead of over-committing.
lucas: i also think batching window amplifies it for longgens (batches combine KV sizes unpredictably). propose lowering max_batch_size for longgen label.
jihoon: plan proposal:
- set model defaults: max_new_tokens=2048, prefetch=false for canary, max_batch_size=2 for longgen route
- runtime guard: if estimated_kv_bytes(request) > 8GB then reject with 4xx and message to lower max_new_tokens
- add per-host memory_reserve_percent=12 for antlia21b instances
- add fallback rule to int8 variant for stability
maya: draft config snippet:
```json
{"model":"antlia21b","defaults":{"max_new_tokens":"2048","prefetch":"false","batching":{"max_batch_size":"2","max_wait_ms":"10"},"memory_reserve_percent":"12"},"fallback_order":["antlia21b-int4","antlia21b-int8"]}
```
emma: add a canary toggle flag so customers that need huge generations can opt-in; must document implications.
lucas: runtime guard should log metrics: rejected_count, avg_estimated_kv, request_id. Also surface to console as a new SLO alert if rejections > 1% of longgen traffic.
infra-bot: deploy plan registered: push config to 6 canary hosts -> monitor OOM rate & rejection metrics for 45m. Auto-rollback if OOM rate increases.
qa-bot: kicking off int8 regression smoke suite on fallback path now. will post diff report. ETA ~15m :hourglass:
maya: if QA looks ok, let's roll at 01:30UTC with ephemeral opt-out. I'll open tiny PR with config + runtime guard + docs note. tagging @emma for review.
emma: LGTM, please include instructions to opt-out per-tenant and add note in model catalog about longgen safe limits. :thumbsup:
